report_name: MoYu Group Abuses Car Head Units for Proxy Botnet

threat_actors.name: MoYu Group
threat_actors.description: A threat actor group linked to a campaign that infects Android-based car head units and incorporates them into a proxy botnet. Previously associated with the BadBox malware operation.

attack_patterns.name: Trusted Relationship
attack_patterns.description: The MoYu Group leveraged the trusted relationship between the device and the pre-installed, legitimate TWCore system application to silently install the JarService malware.

attack_patterns.name: Compromise Host Software Binary
attack_patterns.description: The attackers compromised the legitimate TWCore system application's distribution mechanism to deliver their malicious payload.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Access Software
attack_patterns.description: The JarService malware acts as remote access software, enabling the attackers to turn the infected car head unit into a reverse proxy.

attack_patterns.name: Proxy
attack_patterns.description: The JarService malware configures the infected head unit to act as a reverse proxy, allowing the MoYu Group to route their internet traffic through the vehicle's connection, effectively using it as an exit node.

malware.name: JarService
malware.description: Malware silently installed on Android car head units via the TWCore application. It runs as a background service without a UI, downloads further modules, and turns the vehicle into a reverse proxy node for the MoYu Group's botnet.

malware.name: BadBox
malware.description: A malware operation previously associated with the MoYu Group, indicating a history of compromising Android devices.

tools.name: TWCore
tools.description: A legitimate, pre-installed system application on DoFun head units, intended for analytics and updates, which was abused by the MoYu Group to silently download and install the JarService malware.

identities.name: DoFun
identities.description: A Chinese automotive hardware and software provider whose Android-based in-vehicle infotainment (IVI) systems were targeted in the MoYu Group campaign.

infrastructure.name: MoYu Group Proxy Botnet
infrastructure.description: A botnet of compromised Android car head units used by the MoYu Group as a reverse proxy network to anonymize their internet traffic.
